Module demos and attendance policies and community features reviewed via GitHub collaboration.

## **Employee Self Service Module UI and Mobile Optimization**

* Tom-Blake Asaah recommended using icon cards with modal views on mobile to reduce excessive scrolling.  
* The profile interface requires an avatar upload feature using a placeholder with a plus button.  
* Unbuilt modules will display coming soon placeholders to support structured milestone planning.  
* Attendance interfaces will feature a toggle button to switch between chart views and table views.  
* Salary deduction details will open inside modal windows to maintain a clean interface.  
* The query section will incorporate 3 distinct cards covering open queries, archived queries, and sanctions.  
* Adole Jerome assumed full ownership and training responsibility for the entire ESS module.

## **Attendance Tracking and Geofencing Mechanisms**

* Attendance records connect directly to payroll audits and rule-based wage deductions.  
* Geofencing enforces a 500-meter radius around office locations to flag out-of-radius clock-ins.  
* Employee profiles must display individual work schedules detailing specific remote and onsite shift hours.  
* The system will prompt users to clock in via a modal during their first daily login.  
* The platform will execute automatic clock-outs at the conclusion of each employee shift.

## **Attendance clock-in and clock-out mechanisms**

* The first daily login triggers a modal prompting users to clock in.  
* Users not active on the app are automatically clocked out at 17:00.  
* System sends push notifications at 09:00 to remind users to clock in.  
* Manual clock-in procedures require an active internet connection.  
* Suspended or dismissed employees lose account access and cannot clock in.

## **Device security and enrollment policy**

* Employees can register a maximum of 3 devices for authentication.  
* Clocking in from unregistered devices triggers security flags in attendance tracking.  
* Device enrollment auto-accepts verification without requiring manual HR approval.

## **Attendance policies, deductions, and overtime rules**

* Attendance policy settings include toggles for salary deductions and overtime payments.  
* Overtime rates calculate as an hourly proportion of the daily salary.  
* Employees do not reconcile attendance; queries route for staff justification first.

## **Geofencing work sites**

* Work sites represent official office locations rather than individual employee remote locations.  
* Clocking in within the designated radius classifies the employee as onsite.

## **Staff community and channels**

* Staff community features internal channels for broadcast announcements and direct messaging.  
* Channels support department member additions and automated employee birthday posts.

## **Community Channels and Announcements**

* General channel permissions are set to read-only for HR and CEOs upon creation.  
* System-generated birthday messages automatically display employee avatars or default text from records.  
* Recognition features allow colleagues to highlight individual project contributions across channels.  
* Channel members are accessible through a three-dot menu option on the interface.  
* Announcement dashboards track publish counts, scheduled items, read percentages, and staff audience metrics.

## **Direct Messaging Features**

* Direct messages support one-to-one employee conversations using an integrated employee picker.  
* Users can attach files and send voice notes, while direct calls remain unsupported.

## **Mobile Adaptiveness**

* Mobile layouts use a side drawer for navigation while locking the message composer below.  
* Announcement KPI cards are reduced on mobile views to fit screen constraints properly.

## **Mailbox Module**

* The mailbox module handles basic message sending and receiving without operational links.

## **Engineering Documentation and Guides**

* Engineering guides must be written for individual modules to standardize development practices.  
* Backend architecture documentation requires updates to clarify server-side foundations for developers.

## **Repository Access and Meeting Schedule**

* Collaborators can clone the published GitHub repository to access the current project codebase.  
* The next team meeting is scheduled for the following day between 5:00 PM and 6:00 PM.

### **Summary**

Module demos and attendance policies and community features reviewed via GitHub collaboration.

**Employee Self-Service Demo**  
Adole Jerome demonstrated the Employee Self-Service application and reviewed profile page layouts and mobile optimizations with Tom-Blake Asaah.

**Attendance and Payroll Rules**  
Tom-Blake Asaah and JBS Praxis established attendance tracking mechanisms, geofencing rules, and automated clock-in features.

**Community and Module Ownership**  
Godwin-Okoh Elisha presented the staff community module while Tom-Blake Asaah assigned module ownership and repository tasks.

### **Decisions**

## Aligned

* **Mobile view card and modal layout** Mobile views will utilize card and modal formats to minimize scrolling and text volume.

* **Placeholder display for unbuilt modules** Unbuilt modules will feature a coming soon page indicating the milestone when they become visible.

* **Pagination limit standard for views** The pagination rule is established at 25 items per page across module views.

* **Payroll module visibility setting** The payroll module will be hidden behind an advanced option because employees are treated as contractors and consultants.

* **Profile avatar upload mechanism** Users will upload their profile avatars using a placeholder with a plus button on both mobile and desktop views.

* **Daily attendance clock-in workflow** The system will prompt users to clock in on their first login of each day and automatically clock them out at the end of the day.

* **Automatic clock-out for inactive users** The system will automatically clock out users who are not active on the app at 5:00 PM.

* **First login of the day clock-in prompt** A small UI model will open on a user's first login of the day to ask if they want to clock in directly.

* **Addition of my security tab** A separate 'my security' tab will be added under employee self-service to manage passwords, multi-factor authentication, pass keys, and pins.

* **Mandatory internet connection for clock-in** Users will not be permitted to sign in or clock in without an internet connection.

* **Direct GitHub updates for HTML changes** All front-end HTML modifications must be made directly on the shared GitHub repository.

* **Maximum of three registered devices** Each employee is restricted to registering a maximum of three devices for clocking in.

* **Attendance policy toggles for deductions and overtime** Organization attendance settings must include distinct approval toggles and rules for both salary deductions and overtime payments.

* **Account restriction and absence for suspended employees** Employees who are placed on suspension without pay or dismissed will automatically be considered absent and blocked from accessing their accounts.

* **Manager view for team attendance** Managers will have a feature added to their workspace to view and monitor their specific team members and team attendance.

* **Meeting Time for Tomorrow** The group agreed to schedule tomorrow's meeting between 5:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

* **Notification Settings and Pop-Up Behavior**: JBS Praxis and Tom-Blake Asaah discussed alert notifications, clarifying that push notifications occur outside the app, while strict full-screen modal pop-ups at 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM require direct user confirmation rather than dismissible toasts ([01:44:24](#01:44:24)). JBS Praxis raised the absence of a team attendance view for direct managers, prompting Tom-Blake Asaah to suggest adding a team view under the workspace or homepage using organogram data, as separate menus would clutter the interface ([01:45:49](#01:45:49)).

* **Refining Attendance Policy Settings and Thresholds**: Tom-Blake Asaah questioned placeholders like "still to be confirmed" in the attendance policy settings, instructing that editable fields for grace windows and thresholds, along with deduction and overtime toggles, must be properly structured for the final product ([01:49:29](#01:49:29)). JBS Praxis confirmed understanding of policy edit capabilities ([01:50:31](#01:50:31)).

* **Staff Community Module and Broadcast Channels**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha presented the staff community module, featuring direct messages and announcement channels functioning similarly to WhatsApp broadcast platforms ([01:52:43](#01:52:43)). Godwin-Okoh Elisha demonstrated channel threads, automated birthday announcements generated from employee records, and a plus button used for sharing files, recognizing colleagues, creating polls, or celebrating work anniversaries ([01:54:33](#01:54:33)). Tom-Blake Asaah noted that guidance models describing the plus button functions should be removed from the final UI ([01:55:35](#01:55:35)).

  ![][image11]

* **Channel Creation and Member Access Permissions**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha and Tom-Blake Asaah discussed channel features, with Godwin-Okoh Elisha explaining that clicking a channel displays its message thread on the left and a pop-up modal creates new channels ([01:56:21](#01:56:21)). Tom-Blake Asaah clarified that channels are strictly in-house without public web links, and creators can assign specific departments or members and configure read-and-write permissions ([01:57:23](#01:57:23)).

  ![][image12]

* **Channel Permissions and Automated Birthday Greetings**: Tom-Blake Asaah noted that community announcement channels should be read-only for everyone except HR and the CEO, and pinned to the top of the feed ([01:58:17](#01:58:17)). Additionally, Tom-Blake Asaah proposed an automated birthday greeting system that utilizes employee records to display avatars, custom graphics, and rotating messages ([01:59:03](#01:59:03)).

* **Recognition Feature and Channel Members List Interface**: Tom-Blake Asaah explained that the recognition feature allows staff to acknowledge colleague contributions on projects, which can be posted in standard channels or appear in announcements. Discussing the members list interface, Godwin-Okoh Elisha and Tom-Blake Asaah agreed to replace a direct member button with a three-dot menu that opens a modal for viewing and editing members ([02:00:00](#02:00:00)).

* **Message Composer UI and Screen Layout**: Tom-Blake Asaah stated that the message composer must be fixed on the screen so users do not need to scroll down to access it ([02:00:55](#02:00:55)). This layout change locks the page height and displays the channel name at the top of the interface ([02:01:36](#02:01:36)).

* **Direct Messages and Communication Features**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha described direct messages as one-on-one employee conversations utilizing an employee picker for new messages. Tom-Blake Asaah suggested importing the chat layout and engineering from Praxis while applying their own branding ([02:02:33](#02:02:33)). Furthermore, Tom-Blake Asaah and Godwin-Okoh Elisha confirmed that file attachments and voice notes will be supported, but calling features will be excluded because calls are not yet functional ([02:03:38](#02:03:38)).

* **Announcements Dashboard and KPI Cards**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha outlined the KPI weights cards for announcements, which track four published announcements, one scheduled announcement, average read counts, total staff audience, and monthly posts ([02:04:28](#02:04:28)). Tom-Blake Asaah clarified that the configuration view permits tracking viewed content and right access ([02:05:40](#02:05:40)), while Godwin-Okoh Elisha explained that clicking the plus icon opens a modal for entering announcement headers and bodies, with middleware automatically logging the posting user and date ([02:06:43](#02:06:43)).

* **Mobile Adaptiveness for Channels and Announcements**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha and Tom-Blake Asaah reviewed mobile responsiveness, deciding that channel navigation will open via a side drawer while the active channel takes the full width and length of the mobile screen, with the message composer locked at the bottom. To accommodate mobile view constraints for the five announcement KPI cards, Tom-Blake Asaah and Godwin-Okoh Elisha agreed to reduce the display to four cards by removing the "this month" card ([02:07:30](#02:07:30)) ([02:10:42](#02:10:42)).

* **Demo Updates and Repository Access**: Tom-Blake Asaah instructed Godwin-Okoh Elisha to update the demo before the next meeting, emphasizing that Godwin-Okoh Elisha holds full ownership of the assigned module and will lead client training. Godwin-Okoh Elisha confirmed that the project has been published and collaborators invited to the repository ([02:09:56](#02:09:56)).

* **Mailbox Module Functionality**: Tom-Blake Asaah described the mailbox as a straightforward mail management tool for sending and receiving messages independently of operations ([02:11:28](#02:11:28)). Tom-Blake Asaah and Godwin-Okoh Elisha agreed that the rich text editor composer for the mailbox will be imported from Praxis ([02:12:19](#02:12:19)).

* **Frontend Foundations and Engineering Guides**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha requested that Vos begin working on frontend foundations to provide clear guidance similar to the existing backend structure, and Tom-Blake Asaah directed Godwin-Okoh Elisha to write the backend architecture guide. Tom-Blake Asaah assigned module-specific engineering guides: Godwin-Okoh Elisha for staff community and mailbox, Love for attendance, Tom-Blake Asaah for home, dashboard, and command center, and Victor for employee self-service. Additionally, Tom-Blake Asaah instructed Love to promptly share the meeting transcript and minutes ([02:13:01](#02:13:01)) ([02:14:36](#02:14:36)).

* **Repository Cloning Instructions and Next Meeting Schedule**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha and Tom-Blake Asaah provided instructions for JBS Praxis to clone the repository using VS Code after accepting the GitHub collaboration invite ([02:15:24](#02:15:24)).
